office: Speaker pro tempore, Michigan House of Representatives
label: Written by AI from public sources — may contain errors.

items.t: Said the secretary of state must follow the law, in response to a letter from the Attorney General about subpoenaed election information.
items.q: Rep. Rachelle Smit, R-Martin, responded to a letter from Attorney General Dana Nessel that said some election information requested by subpoena was sensitive, saying the secretary must follow the law.

items.t: Said HB 4983 will turn Michigan's elections into the wild west.
items.q: “Michigan elections are already [in] shambles,” Smit said. “Now, HB 4983 will turn our elections into the wild west.”

items.t: Said placing individuals on the voter rolls automatically without accountability mechanisms will result in thousands of false registrations.
items.q: Automatically placing individuals on the voter rolls without any accountability mechanisms is simply stupid. It will obviously result in thousands of false registrations,” Smit said.

items.t: Said House Republicans are united against the National Popular Vote compact.
items.q: She said House Republicans are united against the National Popular Vote compact, so wavering Democrat support could doom the bills.

record.t: Was elected Speaker Pro Tempore of the Michigan House of Representatives for the One Hundred Third Legislature.
record.q: Resolved by the House of Representatives, That Rachelle Smit is elected to the office of Speaker Pro Tempore of the House of Representatives for the One Hundred Third Legislature.

record.t: Led a House Republican effort to pass a resolution calling on Benson to release records tied to her involvement with the SPLC.
record.q: In May, Smit led a House Republican effort to pass a resolution calling on Benson to release records tied to her involvement with the SPLC.
